section_entries.label: Proof of Theorem 4
section_entries.mathematical_role: Imports a high-moment estimate, applies Holder and maximum-modulus arguments, and combines moment bounds to obtain the stated abundance and zero-free conclusions.

unit_result_entry.title: Combining moment bounds to finish the zero-free abundance conclusions
unit_result_entry.why_material: Theorem 4(i) is said to follow by juxtaposing a lower second-moment fact with a higher-moment bound; for prime modulus a stronger lemma is imported and used to complete Theorem 4(ii).

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: The theorem's abundance and zero-free targets are stated earlier at lines 368-386; this span captures the closing mechanism and prime-specific strengthening.
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: The dependency structure is readable, but the exact powers, counts, and radii require scan verification.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Propagating pointwise moment control across small discs
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The proof deduces successive disc-based bounds, applies the maximum modulus principle to an auxiliary function on a rectangle, relocates the maximum to a controlled boundary point, and applies Lemma 11 to finish the propagation.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: An imported high-moment estimate is reduced with Holder, propagated geometrically using maximum modulus, and combined with a lower-moment fact to obtain the stated Theorem 4 conclusions.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The imported theorem is not proved here, and OCR damage prevents exact recovery of powers, radii, and cardinality thresholds.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Moment control propagated to zero-free conclusions

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The conclusion comes from comparing moments rather than estimating each character separately: aggregate mass is set against a higher-moment cap to force abundance, while the prime-modulus case receives a stronger imported estimate that closes the second conclusion.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Theorem 4(i) is said to follow by combining a fact from Theorem 3(i) with the bound from Lemma 14. When the modulus is prime, Lemma 15 strengthens Lemma 14; it is deduced from a special case of a theorem in the appendix of Ramachandra, restated as Lemma 16, and this completes Theorem 4(ii).
directed.conceptual_reading: The moment comparison is an anti-concentration mechanism: a lower aggregate contribution together with an upper higher-moment bound limits how much mass a few exceptional characters can carry, yielding an abundance conclusion. The prime assumption unlocks a stronger version of that control.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Moment sums bridge analytic size information to a counting or abundance statement; Lemma 14 supplies the general bridge, while the imported prime-specific Lemmas 15-16 replace it when stronger control is available.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The exact moments, powers, counts, radii, and zero-free thresholds are OCR-unsafe, and the prime-specific theorem is imported without proof. The span supports the dependency mechanism but not an exact quantitative reconstruction.
directed.uncertainty: Low for the closing lemma dependencies and prime-specific strengthening; high for all numerical thresholds and for the precise formal deduction of abundance or zero-freeness.
